question: The Sarda River rises in the ________ glacier in the Nepal Himalayas.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Milam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Sarda River originates from the **Milam Glacier** in the Nepal Himalayas.
 
• Milam Glacier is located in the **Pithoragarh district of Uttarakhand, India**.
 
• The glacier is about **16 km long** and lies at an altitude of approximately **3,870 meters above sea level**.
 
• The Sarda River, also known as **Kali or Mahakali River**, forms a part of the India-Nepal border.
 
• The river eventually joins the Ghaghara River, a major left-bank tributary of the Ganges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Himalayan Glaciers:**

 
 
• Glaciers in the Himalayas are crucial sources of freshwater for rivers in the region.
 
• They play a vital role in sustaining the hydrology and ecology of the surrounding areas.
 
 
 
• **Hydrological Importance:**
 
 
• The Sarda River is an important water source for irrigation and hydroelectricity in both India and Nepal.
 
• It supports agriculture and provides drinking water to millions of people.
 
 
 
• **Geopolitical Significance:**
 
 
• The Sarda River forms a natural border between India and Nepal, and there are various treaties and agreements regarding its use.
 
• Both countries collaborate on issues related to water sharing and flood management.
 
 
 
• **Milam Glacier Trek:**
 
 
• The Milam Glacier is a popular trekking destination, attracting adventure enthusiasts from around the world.
 
• The trek offers stunning views of the Himalayan landscape and a chance to explore remote villages.
